rationale: Evidence from race 4 (score 120.36, up from 52.06): progress rose on every track (oval 0.48, s-bend 0.26, slalom 0.125), so kd 0.4 helped the robot cover more of the course. The damping hypothesis for bend oscillation did not hold, though. steering_oscillation on the s-bend rose from 0.139 to 0.202, the slalom stayed at 0.143, and the oval rose from 0.075 to 0.283. The Evaluator's rule says that if bend oscillation does not fall below about 0.139, kd should not be pushed further. I am keeping kd at 0.4 rather than reverting to 0.3, because it is the best measured setting and reverting would likely lose progress. I am not raising kd further. The oval and s-bend failures are now more likely geometric. The sensors sit only 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the robot reacts late on curves. This matches the feedback's second branch: progress stayed near 0.15 on the s-bend while the gains changed, and kd alone has only partly moved it. Change (single lever on geometry): move all five sensor rows forward from y 0.05 to y 0.07, keeping the x values and weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]. The sensors then see the tape roughly 2 cm earlier, which gives the controller more lead on bends. Controller gains, base_speed (1.0), ki (0.2), line_loss and sensor_size (0.012) stay as in race 4, so the race isolates the sensor-position effect. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress rises above 0.26, and oval progress holds near or above 0.48 with oscillation at or below the race-4 level. Completion in 3 s is still not expected at base_speed 1.0. Hypotheses: (a) forward sensors reduce the late-reaction overshoot on bends; (b) if progress does not rise, the drift is a fixed motor mismatch that needs ki above 0.2, and the next test should be ki 0.3 with kd 0.4. Measurements wanted per track and per seed: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, so I can see where each run ends.
